# DeepSeek Harness Linux Desktop
Unofficial Linux x64 desktop port of DeepSeek Harness. This repository maintains an ordered patch se
ries and Linux build, verification and release tools. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepS
and Linux build, verification and release tools. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek.
The default upstream base is read from ci/upstream-base-tag. The recorded verification baseline here
is **`dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1`**. Linux packages bundle **`dsh-scnet@0.6.13`**. Use Actions to check the re
sult for an exact commit.
## Install a published package
The current release is v0.2.2-rc.1-linux.1, built from this repository's six patches against upstrea
m `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1`. Every release here becomes GitHub's latest, because this repository publishes o
ne Linux line; a tag that carries `-rc.` only means its upstream base is a release candidate. Downlo
ad its deb, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig`, or use the installer below. The installer checks the
checksum and amd64 architecture before asking apt to reinstall the package. It needs curl, Node, sha
256sum, dpkg and sudo/apt on the installation host. Verify the signed manifest with `node ci/verify-
release-signature.mjs --manifest SHA256SUMS`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Without `--tag`, the script installs GitHub's latest release, which is the newest build here. Source
changes on main and CI artifacts are separate from published releases. The series in `patches/` is
re-based on `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1` and reduces to six patches: the Linux port, the update gates, the SCNe
t setup actions, the settings-owned update and SCNet actions, the signed release trust path, and the
packaged operation-report worker fix. The plugin operation history, the recovery menus and the upda
te views are upstream in that base and no longer carried as backports.
## Desktop capabilities
| Area | Linux behavior |
| Window and background work | Custom caption, optional native frame, tray/Show Window, and tasks ke

pt running after the last window closes |
| System integration | `dsh` launcher, single-instance rou

ting and registered `dsh://` links |
| Runtime | Linux target payload and bundled WASM Office conver

sion |
| Updates | Settings- and menu-owned check/update actions, verified Linux package download an

d PolicyKit installation; client and Harness are delivered together |
| SCNet | Fixed offline Bundle
/Skill, default Desktop profile activation, preserved explicit disable/custom profile state, and loc

al diagnostics |
| Developer tools | Visible English/Chinese menu and native shortcuts including F12

|
| Recovery | Retrieve a saved crash report, including delayed writes and visible reveal failures

|
| Update dialogs | Owner-attached isolated views, Linux caption/fullscreen handling, cancellation

and mandatory-view recovery |
| SCNet setup repair | External Python uses unpacked files; completion

/errors remain visible in the terminal and spawn failures reject the action |
| Plugin history | Cor
related manager events, a bounded local journal and an isolated report Worker for crash diagnostics

|
| Linux menu actions | Check for Updates uses the release package feed and asks before installing;

Manage dsh Command is available |
| Release trust | `SHA256SUMS` carries an Ed25519 signature verif
ied before a privileged install; a published support floor reports required updates |
The final seven rows describe the source patch series. See desktop follow-up for evidence and remain
ing differences. Real SCNet OAuth2 login is still blocked on its formal service contract and sandbox
credentials. Local diagnostics and an installed Bundle do not establish authorization.
## Build from source
Build on **Linux x86_64**, with Node `>=24.9.0`, pnpm `11.28.5`, Git, build-network access and at le
ast 15 GB free disk. The current upstream workspace may select its own pinned pnpm via package-manag
er management. Cross-building this Linux target from macOS and `linux-arm64` releases are not suppor
s-building this Linux target from macOS and `linux-arm64` releases are not supported by this series.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use a fresh `$SRC`. `apply.sh` checks out the pinned upstream tag, creates the Linux branch, applies
every `patches/*.patch` in filename order with **`git apply --3way`**, and creates `.env.linux`. Ch
anges are staged; they are not one commit per patch. Record the patched source with `git -C "$SRC" w
rite-tree`; `HEAD` still names the upstream base. Build details, paths and troubleshooting are in th
EAD` still names the upstream base. Build details, paths and troubleshooting are in the Linux guide.
## Verification and release
PRs and relevant main pushes apply the series, typecheck the full workspace, run focused desktop reg
ressions, build the deb, audit the SCNet payload, and install/start that same candidate on Ubuntu 24
.04 under Xvfb. Draft pull requests do not start that job, and a newer push cancels an in-flight pul
l-request run, so work in progress cannot mail a failure for a commit that was already replaced. The
ordinary second-launch window assertion is skipped in this headless session; it needs a real deskto
p. Published-byte verification, upgrades, AppArmor, Wayland and Debian 13 are separate manual jobs.
A skipped job is not a passed platform check.
PR #5 passed 254 desktop regressions, full typecheck, packaging and installed-session checks in run
41273560891; the merged main was also verified in run 41274912984. The SCNet setup repair and biling
ual docs then passed run 41278271808 with 268 desktop tests and documentation run 41278271805. The `
dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1` series needs its own green publish run before it becomes a release; the evidence re
corded so far is in the desktop follow-up.
Publishing is manual through publish-linux-desktop.yml. It pins the build commit, records the staged
patched tree, audits and installs the built bytes, signs the checksum manifest with the release key
and publishes the deb, the signed manifest, the support policy and the checksums. Verify published
bytes with `node ci/verify-release-signature.mjs --manifest SHA256SUMS`. Upstream synchronization cr
eates reviewable PRs and never merges or publishes; a fresh upstream patch conflict is recorded as a
n issue instead of a failed scheduled run. See sync operations.
